title: Adivasi students who walked from Nashik detained in Mumbai before an Azad Maidan protest

tea.why: Students say tribal residential (ashram) schools lack basic facilities and scholarships are delayed.
tea.want: Better facilities in ashram schools, timely scholarships, and the tribal development minister's resignation (Congress demand).
tea.changed: Oct 5: students sheltering at the Congress office in Dadar were picked up by police; police deny arresting them.

summary: A group of Adivasi students who had protested in Nashik and then travelled on foot and by other means to Mumbai planned to protest at Azad Maidan over poor facilities in tribal residential schools and delayed scholarships. The Congress gave them shelter at its Dadar headquarters on the night of October 4. The party says police entered the office in the early hours of October 5 and took the students away to stop the protest; Maharashtra Congress president Harshvardhan Sapkal and MP Varsha Gaikwad called it unlawful and demanded the resignation of the Tribal Development Minister and the department's commissioner. The students said police had not answered their request for permission. Police denied arresting the students, Deccan Chronicle reported.
demands: Basic facilities in tribal ashram schools
Resignation of the Tribal Development Minister (Congress demand)
response: Police denied arresting the students, according to Deccan Chronicle; the students said police did not respond to their request to protest at Azad Maidan.

crowd.text: hundreds of students, according to the Maharashtra Congress

updates.text: Students who had walked from Nashik stayed overnight at the Congress office in Dadar.
Congress says police took the students from its office before dawn; police deny arresting them.
